description: Tombs of Terror bosses B (phase 8 family 20): eighteen encounters of Saviors of Uldum's Tombs of Terror (ULDA_BOSS_19 to ULDA_BOSS_36: Sothis, Kham, Illidara Sunsdawn, Colossus of the Sun, Skarik, Suspicious Palm Tree, Beetle Herder Zenda, Thudd Lockspring, Ol' Toomba, Sazin, Ozara, Ermavar, Pillager Drasar, Edra, Runaway Ruby, Dovo Fastfuse, Earthrager Ptah, Kasa Softspeaker). Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves the names against facts/violet-hold-2026-09.json, checks every card and writes data/dungeon-run/encounters-v1.json. Every Tombs boss hero prints 10 Health: Health is the act curve's, and the tier is the boss's level band read from its page's deck table (levels 1-2: tier 1; 2-3 and 3-4: tier 2; 5-6: tier 3; 7: tier 4; verify/tools/gen/p8f19/tombs_tiers.py, family 19's rule).
method: Each page's wikitext (action=raw) was read and its deck table expanded (rowspans and colspans) into a grid; the Normal and Heroic columns are transcribed in table order with their counts (25 or 30 cards); a table of possible cards without counts ("10; 15", "15; 20", Skarik's) is transcribed with count null. Where the Normal list is shorter than 30 the Heroic table is transcribed too and is the row's extend list. A page's level note ("These decks correspond only to level N") and its chapter line are recorded in the row's schedule adaptation. The file is written by verify/tools/gen/p8f20/make_f20.py.

"Retired" Treasure Hunter (2) puts a copy of a random card of the run player's hand into the boss's hand, with the card's in-hand enchantments (Mind Vision's rule, the power's template). The boss learns that one card: the copy is its own; the run player sees which card was copied. In the boss's fair-view search the run player's hand holds only masked cards, so there the copy is made only from a card the boss already saw go into that hand (else nothing): the search never reads the hidden hand. Offered while the run player's hand (a public count) holds a card and the boss's hand has room.

Mighty Windstorm (0): each player, the boss first, swaps a random minion of their hand with a random minion of their board: the board minion returns to its owner's hand (as a fresh card) and the hand minion is put onto the board in its place (summoned, so no Battlecry). A player with no minion in hand or none on board swaps nothing. A run shrine is never chosen (a run shrine never leaves the board). The run player's hand minion becomes public as it is summoned; the hidden hand is not read for anything else, and in the boss's fair-view search that hand holds only masked cards, so there the run player swaps only a minion the boss already saw go into that hand. The wiki's Hero Power table marks it Auto-cast and the client card carries AI_MUST_PLAY, so it is cast by rule, not by a choice of the boss's AI (DungeonRunEncounters.AutoCast, family 09's rule; the close-out review): at the start of the boss's turn, after the draw, while the boss can swap (its own hand and board) or the run player has a minion on board and a card in hand (public facts).

Madness Incarnate (1): the boss's hero gains +1 Attack this turn (enchantment ULDA_BOSS_36e), then attacks up to three different random enemy minions, one after another (forced attacks: a frozen or exhausted hero attacks too, a Taunt does not redirect, a Stealthed or Immune minion is not picked, a minion that died is not picked; the hero takes each minion's damage, an equipped weapon loses Durability, and the attacks stop when either hero dies). Offered while the run player has a minion it can attack.
